xkeyboard-config: drop brokenbar from Swiss (German) layout Historically, the Swiss (German) layout has had two vertical bar characters: * Senkrechter Strich (U+007C, vertical line) * Unterbrochener Strich (U+00A6, broken bar) The broken bar is a relic from old school mechanical typesetting to have a character that looked different from uppercase-I and lowercase-l. Nowadays, the character does not have use for a typical user and only serves as a point of confusion when shells treat it differently from the regular vertical bar. For what it's worth, upstream xkeyboard-config and Mac OS X do not have this character in their layout. Windows appears to still have the character (at least in Windows 7). In the interest of reducing the number of Chrome OS specific patches to xkeyboard-config and reducing user confusion, we should drop this patch. Thanks to ricop@ on eng-misc for helping explain the historical context of this character. BUG=chromium:969208 BRANCH=none TEST=emerged xkeyboard-config, observed patch was not applied Change-Id: Id8651997d0dc42a138870182913163c793e00690 Signed-off-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1713838 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
